_comment: Pinned facts for an ELIGIBLE azure-to-aws fast-path Clarify (clarify.md Step 0.5) over the hand-authored estate in after-clarify-fast-path/. The committed Terraform corpus is ineligible by design, so this is the only golden where the fast-path provenance contract (clarify-assemble.md Fast-path mode; schema-preferences.md metadata) is exercised. Same selection rule as the sibling specs: only facts where a plausible improvisation and the correct answer DIVERGE.
_limitation: This tests BRANCHING and the metadata contract, not conversation. The estate is hand-authored, not algorithm-traced: its inventory and clusters were written to satisfy the eligibility rule, not produced by a Discover run.

global.target_region.why: every resource is westeurope, so the region is MAPPED from the estate, not proposed.

design_constraints.compliance.why: Compliance is never inferable, so it is the one question every fast-path estate is asked. It is ANSWERED here ([] = explicit none) because the fast path asks ESSENTIAL rows first; a null here would mean the short path skipped a question it promised to ask.

design_constraints.cpu_architecture.why: no Windows anywhere, so x86_64 is a CHOICE this time (the Terraform corpus forces it). PROPOSED with the x86_64 default, and the default must be listed in questions_defaulted because nobody was asked.

design_constraints.compute_target.why: the fast path applied the documented default without a sheet. It must still read PROPOSED and must be listed in questions_defaulted — the Estimate block is where the user first sees it.

design_constraints.vm_cutover.why: no VM, so the one ESSENTIAL row with no defensible default does not fire. If it did, the estate would be ineligible (has_vm) and the fast path could not have been offered.

data.availability.why: no HA signal on the source (enrichment skipped; the eligibility rule's has_ha_database is false), so Q-D1 is PROPOSED at single-az. ESSENTIAL would make the estate ineligible; DETECTED would read a posture the capture never saw.

data.db_cutover.why: a relational database with NO measured size. Q-D2's unknown-size branch applies: dump_restore (the runbook with no AWS charge), size_coverage unknown, largest_relational_db_gib null, a basis that says the size was not measured. The plausible wrong answers are an invented size, an escalation to ESSENTIAL (which would add a question the fast-path offer promised not to ask), or dms (which would invent DMS instance hours).

data.cosmos_rw_split.why: no Cosmos account; written as N/A with a reason, not omitted.

baseline.azure_monthly_spend.why: no billing source was discovered, so Q-A5 is the second and last fast-path question; it is answered here. This is what makes [N] = 2 in the Step 0.5 offer.

identity.why: Category J ALWAYS fires; on the fast path its default is applied and listed in questions_defaulted.

app_service_plans[0].isolation_split.why: THE row this golden exists for. One Linux plan hosts two apps, so Q-C2 fires as PROPOSED with the no-split default and is NOT asked on the fast path. clarify.md's isolation postcondition and clarify-assemble.md's checklist must accept this — the row carries its default, is listed under its index key in questions_defaulted, and is disclosed at estimate-assemble.md Step 2. A GATE_FAIL here is the finding this spec reproduces.

row_dispositions._requires_keys_why: requires_keys follows the DISPOSITION, per schema-preferences.md: DETECTED needs `source`, N/A needs `reason`, ESSENTIAL needs `context`. db_cutover additionally needs default_basis and size_coverage on both Clarify paths.

essential_gate._why: Both ESSENTIAL rows the fast path can fire (compliance, spend) were asked first and answered, so the phase COMPLETES. An unanswered ESSENTIAL here would mean the fast path defaulted a row it has no default for.

clarify_mode._why: Discover marked this estate eligible (no VM, no licensing signal, no Cosmos Core, no HA database, one region, 1 cluster, 5 resources) and the user took the offer, so clarify_mode is fast_path and fast_path_eligible is copied from the inventory as true.
clarify_mode._deferred_why: A relational database is present, so db_cutover is defaulted-and-deferred and metadata.deferred_to_generate names it — and ONLY that list does; see fast_path_provenance.

fast_path_provenance._why: On the fast path every PROPOSED row that took its default without being asked must be listed in metadata.questions_defaulted (array rows under index keys) so estimate-assemble.md Step 2 can render the 'Assumptions behind this number' block and clarify.md's mode-aware gates can pass. ESSENTIAL rows were ASKED and the deferred row is asked at Step 3b, so neither may appear there — a deferred row in both lists renders twice and leaves Step 3b two entries to clear.

db_cutover_default_rule._why: The default is not a fixed pin but Q-D2's RULE evaluated against the inventory's relational storage_mb. Here NO relational server carries storage_mb (enrichment row 7 skipped), so the rule must yield dump_restore with size_coverage unknown and largest_relational_db_gib null. Inventing a size so the two-branch rule fires, or escalating to ESSENTIAL, are the improvisations this pins against.

defaults_not_promoted._why: A value taken from its default must still read PROPOSED. On the fast path EVERY PROPOSED row took its default, so this is the path where a promotion to DETECTED is most tempting and most wrong.

isolation_rows._why: One plan, two apps. Keyed by azure_id because a live-sourced inventory has no tf_address. The disposition must be PROPOSED (a real question with a default), never N/A (that is the 0- and 1-app answer) and never ESSENTIAL (it has a documented default).

/subscriptions/<subscription-fixture>/re.why: two apps share the plan; the default is no split and it is disclosed with its cost consequence next to the estimate.

licensing_firing._why: No Windows VM, no Microsoft.Sql/*, no SQL-on-VM signature, so the licensing fragment does not load. It must be written as an EXPLICIT N/A with a reason (clarify-assemble.md Assembly rule 3), never omitted — and if it HAD fired the estate would be ineligible (has_licensing_signal).

cluster_rows._why: preferences.clusters[] must key exactly to the clusters artifact (one cluster here).

forbidden_substrings._why: preferences has no reason to hold even app-setting NAMES, let alone values.
